title: Geometry of finite normalized point-blowup towers
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian excellent scheme of finite Krull dimension $d\geq1$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], where Noetherian means a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings and excellence is imposed on every affine open. Put $X_0=X^\nu$, the normalization of $X$ in its function field [def-sc-normalization, def-sc-function-field]. Given a finite tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0$ in which each arrow is the blowup at a reduced closed point followed by normalization in its function field [def-nagata-global-blowup], every $X_j$ is integral, normal, excellent, Noetherian, and of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. All normalization morphisms used here are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The composite $X_n\to X$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] and induces an isomorphism of function fields. If $U\subseteq X$ is a normal open subscheme and every chosen center maps into $X\setminus U$, the restriction $X_n\times_X U\to U$ is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular, for $n=0$ normalization is an isomorphism over every normal open. No regularity of $X_n$ and no existence of a tower with regular endpoint is asserted.

proof.text: First consider any integral Noetherian excellent scheme $T$. Its componentwise normalization is precisely its function-field normalization: on a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$, there is one minimal prime, namely $(0)$, so the affine-chart lemma gives $\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$, with $A\subseteq\overline A\subseteq k(T)$. The normalization-preparation theorem gives a finite surjective map $\nu_T:T^\nu\to T$, a normal Noetherian excellent source, and an isomorphism over a dense open. The source is integral: each nonempty chart $\operatorname{Spec}\overline A$ is integral because $\overline A$ is a subring of a field. Its generic point is the zero prime, and these points agree on overlaps under the normalization construction; every nonempty such chart contains this point. Thus the entire source is irreducible and reduced. Moreover $\operatorname{Frac}\overline A=\operatorname{Frac}A=k(T)$, since the two inclusions $A\subseteq\overline A\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}A$ give both inclusions between their fraction fields. The affine function-field lemma identifies this equality with the map on scheme function fields.

source.place: Tags 035Q, 035S and the affine description of normalization.

proof.text: The finite map $\nu_T$ is projective in the projective-bundle convention by the finite-projectivity lemma, hence proper by the projective-bundle properness lemma. The preceding step makes it dominant and gives a degree-one extension of function fields. Apply the closed-dominant dimension theorem (target $T$ locally Noetherian, map locally of finite type and closed because proper): its transcendence-degree term is zero, so $\dim T^\nu=\dim T$. This applies to $T=X$ and will also apply to every ordinary blowup below.

For later use, normalization is unchanged over any normal open $V\subseteq T$. On a nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq V$, take $c\in\overline A\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}A$ and write $c=a/s$ with $s\ne0$. It is a section on the dense open $D(s)\subseteq W$, integral over $A$. Apply the integral-section extension lemma to the normal locally Noetherian scheme $W$, its affine open $W$ and dense open $D(s)$: $c$ extends to an element of $A$. Equality can be tested in the function field by the affine function-field description. Hence $\overline A=A$. The normalization-chart lemma identifies $\nu_T^{-1}W\to W$ with the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. These inverse maps agree on overlaps because two inverses to a fixed morphism are equal, so they glue to an inverse over $V$. The empty open causes no exception.

source.place: Tag 035K and normalization over the normal locus; the cited integral-section extension supplies the normal-ring argument.

proof.text: We now induct on the number $j$ of chosen normalized point blowups. The induction assertion is that $X_j$ is integral, normal, Noetherian and excellent, has dimension $d$, that all normalizations so far are finite, and that the composite $X_j\to X$ is projective and induces the identity extension of function fields. Steps 1 and 2 with $T=X$ establish all these assertions for $j=0$. Suppose they hold for $j$. A reduced closed point $x\in X_j$ is different from the generic point, since $\dim X_j=d\ge1$. Therefore its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_x$ is nonzero (at the generic point it is the unit ideal). The closed subscheme ideal is quasi-coherent, and on each Noetherian affine open its ideal is finitely generated. Apply the ordinary-blowup geometry lemma to obtain an integral $B=\operatorname{Bl}_{x}(X_j)$ and a projective map $b:B\to X_j$.

The projective-bundle properness lemma makes $b$ proper, and hence of finite type. By the finite-type definition, over each affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X_j$ its inverse image admits a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $A$-algebras. Each coordinate ring in that cover is excellent by finite-type stability of excellence and thus Noetherian. Starting with the finite affine cover of $X_j$, these finitely many inverse-image covers give a finite affine cover of $B$. Thus $B$ is Noetherian. The excellence affine-cover theorem gives excellence on every affine open of $B$. This uses no affine-base or ample-line-bundle hypothesis on $X_j$.

source.place: Tag 0BFT proof: finite-type stability; more-algebra Tag 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent).

proof.text: The complement-of-center theorem identifies $b^{-1}(X_j\setminus\{x\})\to X_j\setminus\{x\}$ with an isomorphism. This open contains the generic point, so $b$ is dominant and induces an isomorphism of function fields. The closed-dominant dimension theorem applies to the proper map $b$ between integral schemes, with locally Noetherian target $X_j$ and transcendence-degree term zero. It gives $\dim B=\dim X_j=d$. Apply Steps 1 and 2 to this integral Noetherian excellent $B$. Its normalization $X_{j+1}\to B$ is finite and projective, its source is integral normal Noetherian excellent of dimension $d$, and its function field is still $k(X_j)=k(X)$.

Every Noetherian scheme just obtained is quasi-compact from its finite affine cover and is quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness lemma. Apply projective-bundle composition first over the qcqs base $X_j$ to $X_{j+1}\to B\to X_j$, and then over the qcqs base $X$ to $X_{j+1}\to X_j\to X$. Both composites are projective. Their function-field maps are compositions of the isomorphisms in Step 6 and the induction hypothesis. This completes the inductive step, so the assertions hold for each $j\le n$.

Finally suppose the chosen centers all map outside the given normal open $U\subseteq X$. Step 3 gives $X_0\times_XU\simeq U$. Inductively let $V_j=X_j\times_XU\simeq U$. The next center is disjoint from $V_j$, so the complement-of-center theorem makes $B\times_{X_j}V_j\to V_j$ an isomorphism. Its source is therefore normal. Step 3 applied to the normalization $X_{j+1}\to B$ shows that this normalization is also an isomorphism on that open of $B$. Composing gives $X_{j+1}\times_XU\simeq V_j\simeq U$. Induction proves the required restriction for $j=n$, including $n=0$. This is an induction on a supplied tower; it constructs no regular endpoint.
